text:
maya (PM): Heads up — I need a short PRD + acceptance criteria for a serving fallback strategy that covers kernel incompatibilities + KV cache miss storms for a large enterprise pilot. Want a solid rollout plan and monitoring contract by EOD Friday.

chris (eng-runtime): Got it. Quick q: what SLA targets are we promising to the customer so we can drive tradeoffs?

maya (PM): Customer asks: 99.9% uptime, p95 <= 250ms for short sequences (<=128 tokens), p99 <= 800ms. They also want bounded quality regressions on their prompt set — no more than 10% relative drop in their primary eval metric when we fallback.

liam (SRE): We need concrete definitions: "quality" metric must be a numeric signal (e.g., correctness score from their eval harness or embedding cosine for rerank). Also confirm which model families are in scope (Llama2-style, Mistral variants?).

dina (ML infra): They're primarily on llama2-13B and a custom fine-tuned 7B. I propose the acceptance rule: any fallback path that moves from baseline kernel/quant to an alternate kernel/quant must keep delta_metric >= -2% absolute or fail fast. If it fails, we must route to higher-tier nodes rather than silently serving lower quality.

samir (englead): Edge cases I care about: long-sequence (>2048) sessions where KV cache is essential; when cache misses spike (e.g., after instance restarts) we could hit p99s. Fallbacks must include an ordered chain: (1) compatible kernel variant on same node, (2) route to warm spare pool with original kernel, (3) degrade batch size / increase CPU offload as last resort. Need cost guardrails.

chris (eng-runtime): Drafting acceptance criteria list here:
- Functional: fallback chain must preserve API semantics and deterministic behavior for same random seed.
- Latency: for traffic routed to fallback, p95 must remain <= 250ms for <=128 tokens, otherwise immediate failover to spare pool.
- Quality: run customer eval harness on rollout canary (10k prompts) — regression <= 2% absolute on primary metric.
- Observability: emit runtime metrics: `runtime.fallback.count`, `runtime.fallback.reason`, `runtime.kernel.variant`, `runtime.kv.cache.hit_rate`, `runtime.quality.regression.delta`.
- Tracing: requests using fallback must be traceable in the Console with `fallback=true`.

maya (PM): Nice. Also add acceptance for rollback criteria: if we see >0.5% of global traffic with regression >2% for 15m, auto-roll back the rollout.

liam (SRE): For monitoring contract, add concrete thresholds and dashboards:
- `p95_latency` per route and per kernel variant alert: warn at 200ms, sev at 250ms.
- `fallback.rate` warn at 1% of route traffic, sev at 3%.
- `quality.regression.delta` warn at -1.5%, sev at -2%.
- Create a synthetic canary job that continuously evaluates 500 samples / 5m and posts to the Console.

dina (ML infra): Implementation notes: kernel selection is decided at routing time using a compatibility matrix. Example config: \n```json\n{"fallback_chain": ["kernel-v2-fast-attn", "kernel-v1-compat", "route:spare-pool"], "quality_threshold_pct": 2.0, "latency_p95_ms": 250}\n```\nWe need a CI job that runs the customer eval on kernel variants and produces a diff artifact we can attach to rollouts.

samir (englead): Tests: add unit tests for kernel compatibility detection, integration test that simulates KV cache cold-start with synthetic traffic, and load test with spike to verify fallback ramping. Also a chaos test that kills warm nodes to reproduce cache miss storms.

chris (eng-runtime): Rollout plan (high level):
1) Feature flag gated in console for the customer (canary=1%).
2) Run synthetic eval harness in CI and Console.
3) Canary to 5% with active monitoring for 30m.
4) If metrics green, ramp 25% -> 100% over 6hr with pause windows.
5) Auto-roll back on triggers (latency, fallback.rate, quality delta).

maya (PM): Who owns what?
- chris: PRD + runtime config API + compatibility matrix.
- dina: CI eval pipeline + quality regression job.
- liam: monitoring dashboards, alerts, rollback automation.
- samir: test plan + load/chaos validation.
Target: first internal canary by next Tue.

liam (SRE): I'll add Datadog queries and a Console dashboard template. cc @dina for eval job sinks.

chris (eng-runtime): Quick open questions:
- Do we allow kernel-level quantized fallbacks (e.g., int4) by default, or must that be opt-in per customer? quant fallbacks can reduce cost but risk quality.

maya (PM): Customer is risk-averse. Make quantized fallbacks opt-in. Default fallback chain should prefer compatible float kernels, then reduced-capacity nodes, then opt-in quant.

dina (ML infra): Note: some kernels don't support certain attention optimizations for very long sequences; we should annotate compatibility matrix with (max_seq_len, max_kv_entries) so routing can enforce safe cutovers.

samir (englead): Also include billing visibility: when we route to spare pool or high-tier nodes during fallbacks, surface incremental cost to the Console and to billing alerts. Customer expects cost transparency.

chris (eng-runtime): I'll attach a minimal RFC doc draft after this thread. Will add sample config and API shape for `fallback_policy` and `compatibility_matrix`.

deploy-bot: scheduled: "canary-eval-job" started for customer-pilot at 1998765800

maya (PM): Thanks. If we can get the PRD + acceptance criteria in the doc by EOD Friday I can start customer sign-off. We'll iterate but this is the core contract we ship to sales/CS.

samir (englead): Agree. I'll prep test stories in the sprint board.

chris (eng-runtime): +1. Will post RFC link here when ready."
